subject: Segmented deletion attestation & SIG mapping request
messages:
From: Helen Park <hpark@medarc.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: MedArc Security <security@medarc.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0500
Subject: Request: segmented deletion attestation + SIG mapping

Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. MedArc is moving toward finalizing our SIG/CAIQ submission this week and we need two items from Redwood to close our path to procurement: 1) an attestation that Redwood can perform tenant-scoped (segmented) deletion of inference/session logs with a per-tenant TTL policy and 2) a mapping file showing where SIG controls related to data retention/deletion and audit logging are satisfied by Redwood artifacts and evidence.

Scope notes: this is specific to our production tenant (tenant-id: medarc-prod-01) and applies to session logs and inference traces (not model weights). We may request a short-term hold for forensics later, but for now the ask is a standard deletion attestation and control mapping.

Deliverables we'd like by EOD Thursday (2026-11-26):
- A one-page deletion attestation stating retention windows and the deletion workflow for the tenant (PDF)
- A SIG/CAIQ mapping CSV with references to artifacts (SOC 2 report pages, retention config screenshots, sample audit export)
- List of any customer-specific exceptions required to meet our regulatory posture

Can you confirm? If you need a short call to align on artifacts, happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Head of Security Operations
MedArc Health

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the clear scope. We can provide both items and have a proposed delivery plan below. Quick clarifications before we finalize the pack:

1) For the attestation, do you require notarization or just an internal Redwood exec-signed PDF? (Most customers accept a signed company attestation; we can escalate to an exec sign-off if you need legal notarization.)

2) When you say "inference traces," can you confirm whether you need deletion proof for KV cache traces and runtime telemetry (request/response bodies) or only the trimmed session-level metadata? We can produce evidence for all three buckets but will need to map to the relevant SIG controls differently.

Proposed deliverables/timeline (targeting your Thursday EOD):
- Draft deletion-attestation-draft.pdf (internal legal + compliance review) — Wed EOD 11/24
- SIG/CAIQ mapping CSV (sig-control-mapping.csv) with column links to artifacts — Thu morning 11/26
- Evidence bundle (sample audit export, screenshots, short video of deletion in lower env) — Thu EOD 11/26

Irene and Priyom are copied to scope the artifacts and run the export. If that timeline is too aggressive, we can push one business day.

Next steps: Priyom — can you pull a sample audit export and an example of the tenant retention config and add them to the Drive link? Irene — will you and I double-check the attestation language for SOC 2 alignment?

Helen — happy to jump on a 30-min call today if helpful; otherwise we'll proceed and share the draft by Wed.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Jonas / Irene —

I pulled a sample export from medarc-prod-01 (redacted) and the tenant TTL config. Dropped the following files into the shared Drive folder:
- medarc_sample_audit_export.csv (redacted IDs)
- tenant-ttl-config-screenshot.png
- deletion-playbook.md (internal runbook excerpt)

Notes:
- The runtime telemetry includes three layers: request metadata, ephemeral KV cache, and full request/response bodies. Our standard retention window for request/response bodies in production is 30 days unless customer requests a shorter TTL.
- For segmented deletion we support per-tenant TTL plus an on-demand deletion call that issues a targeted erasure job. The erasure job updates the object index, triggers secure deletion across warm/cold storage, and emits a deletion audit event.

I'll prepare the sig-control-mapping.csv with explicit references to SOC 2 sections and the sample export lines that show the deletion audit event format. Expect a first pass by EOD Wed 11/25.

- Priyom

Helen —

Attached is the deliverable pack we discussed. Highlights:
- deletion-attestation-draft.pdf — one-page attestation signed by our Head of Compliance. It states: MedArc tenant (medarc-prod-01) is configured for tenant-scoped TTL; standard request/response body retention is 30 days; on-demand tenant deletion will remove session logs and inference traces within a bounded job (typically completes within 48 hours for tenant of this size) and emits a deletion audit event.
- sig-control-mapping.csv — maps SIG/CAIQ questions related to data retention and logging to our artifacts (SOC 2 report page refs, sample audit lines, config screenshots). We called out the controls where a customer-specific exception is necessary (e.g., if you require <7 day retention for request bodies, we will need a config change and a SLA addendum).
- segmented-deletion-plan.xlsx — step-by-step of the erasure job plus proof checkpoints (audit event samples included).

Notes and exceptions:
- If you need retention <7 days for request/response bodies, that is considered a customer-specific configuration and requires a short SLAs/commitment — we flagged that in the CSV.
- For notarized attestations, we can accommodate but will need legal to approve and it may add 3–5 business days.

Helen, please confirm receipt and whether the attestation language is acceptable for your procurement packet. If you'd like an exec sign-off, we can route it tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
